script.title: OOMKilled ke fixes, ranked

dialogue.speaker: budhdev
dialogue.text: Hamari Node API Kubernetes par baar baar OOMKilled ho rahi thi. Criterion ek hi: crash band ho, aur memory bhi barbaad na ho.

dialogue.speaker: budhdev
dialogue.text: Limit hi hata do? Pod node ki saari memory kha sakta hai aur baaki pods ko bhi gira dega. Seedha F.

dialogue.speaker: budhdev
dialogue.text: Har raat pods restart karo. Crash thoda kam dikhega, par leak wahin ka wahin. D tier.

dialogue.speaker: budhdev
dialogue.text: Memory limit badha do. Abhi ke liye theek, par leak hai toh bas thodi der se crash hoga. C tier.

dialogue.speaker: budhdev
dialogue.text: Ab Node ka max old space size, container ki limit se thoda kam. Yeh kitna kaam ka hai?

pause.prompt: Node's --max-old-space-size is set a bit below the container's memory limit. What does that change?
choices: Node collects garbage harder before the kernel kills the pod

dialogue.speaker: budhdev
dialogue.text: Node limit ke paas pahunchne se pehle hi zor se garbage collection karta hai, kernel ke maarne se pehle. A tier.

dialogue.speaker: budhdev
dialogue.text: Aur leak dhoondh ke code theek karna, jaise kabhi na saaf hone wala cache. Asli ilaaj yahi hai. S tier.

script.takeaway: Find the leak; until then, keep Node's heap limit below the container limit so it collects garbage before the kernel kills it.

questions.prompt: Why is removing the memory limit F tier?
choices: One leaking pod can eat the node's memory and take other pods down
questions.explanation: Without a limit the leak grows until the whole node runs out of memory.
